from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Slope vs. Area", [
            "Derivatives measure the slope of a curve.",
            "Integrals calculate the area under a curve.",
            "These two concepts seem completely unrelated."
        ])

        # Assets
        area_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/area.svg").set_color("#FF00FF")
        slope_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/slope.svg").set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(area_icon, 'A5', scale_factor=0.4)
        self.place_at_grid(slope_icon, 'A6', scale_factor=0.4)

        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 5, 1], y_range=[-1, 5, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'C2', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        func = lambda x: 0.2 * x**2 + 0.5
        graph = axes.plot(func, color=WHITE)
        
        x_val = ValueTracker(1)
        point = Dot(color="#00FFFF")
        point.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(axes.c2p(x_val.get_value(), func(x_val.get_value()))))
        
        # Manually create tangent line using standard Line
        tangent = Line(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color="#00FFFF")
        def update_tangent(l):
            x = x_val.get_value()
            slope = 0.4 * x
            angle = np.arctan(slope)
            l.rotate(angle - l.get_angle())
            l.move_to(axes.c2p(x, func(x)))
            
        tangent.add_updater(update_tangent)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(graph), FadeIn(slope_icon))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(Create(point), Create(tangent))
        self.play(x_val.animate.set_value(3), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        area = axes.get_area(graph, x_range=[0, 2], color="#FF00FF", opacity=0.5)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"), FadeIn(area_icon))
        self.play(Create(area))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Accumulation Function", [
            "Define an accumulation function for area.",
            "The sweep visualizes area growth.",
            "Growth rate equals curve height."
        ])
        
        # Axes and Function
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 3, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        axes.set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=0.55)
        self.add(axes)
        
        f = lambda t: 0.5 * (t - 1)**2 + 1
        curve = axes.plot(f, x_range=[0.5, 3.5], color="#FFFFFF")
        self.add(curve)
        
        # Asset: Scanner
        scanner = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/scanner.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(scanner, "A6", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(FadeIn(scanner))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        area_func_label = MathTex(r"A(x) = \int_a^x f(t)dt", font_size=30).set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(area_func_label, "B6", scale_factor=0.75)
        self.play(Write(area_func_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        
        x_tracker = ValueTracker(1)
        sweep_line = always_redraw(lambda: axes.get_vertical_line(axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), 0), line_func=Line, color="#00FFFF"))
        self.add(sweep_line)
        
        # Area fill
        area = always_redraw(lambda: axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0.5, x_tracker.get_value()], color="#00FFFF", opacity=0.3))
        self.add(area)
        
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(3.0), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        
        # Asset: Hourglass
        hourglass = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/hourglass.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(hourglass, "F6", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(FadeIn(hourglass))
        
        height_line = always_redraw(lambda: Line(axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), 0), axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), f(x_tracker.get_value())), color="#FF0000", stroke_width=4))
        self.add(height_line)
        
        rate_label = MathTex(r"A'(x) = f(x)", font_size=30).set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(rate_label, "D6", scale_factor=0.75)
        self.play(Write(rate_label))
        
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(1.0), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Formalizing the Connection", [
            "Derivatives undo integration of functions.", 
            "This formalizes the inverse relationship.", 
            "They are perfect mathematical opposites."
        ])
        
        # Setup formula
        # d/dx [∫_{a}^{x} f(t)dt] = f(x)
        formula = MathTex(
            r"\frac{d}{dx}", 
            r"\left[", 
            r"\int_{a}^{x}", 
            r"f(t)", 
            r"dt", 
            r"\right]", 
            r"=", 
            r"f(x)"
        )
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'C3', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Load dummy assets
        icon1 = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg")
        icon2 = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(icon1, 'B6', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(icon2, 'E6', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Write(formula), FadeIn(icon1))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight d/dx (Green)
        self.play(formula[0].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Highlight Integral (Cyan)
        self.play(formula[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show substitution f(x) (Yellow)
        self.play(formula[7].animate.set_color("#FFCC00"))
        
        # Final box
        box = SurroundingRectangle(formula, color=WHITE, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(box, 'C3', 'D4', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Create(box), FadeIn(icon2))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Compute areas without infinite sums.", "Use anti-derivatives for simpler results.", "Subtraction solves the definite integral."]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Application", lecture_lines)
        
        # Prepare animation elements

        summary = Text("Fundamental Theorem of Calculus", font_size=24, color=WHITE)

            MathTex(r"\int_{a}^{b} f(x) dx = F(b) - F(a)"),

outline.topic: The Fundamental Bridge: The Relationship Between Integrals and Derivatives

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Slope vs. Area
sections.content: Briefly revisit the derivative as the slope of a tangent line (rate of change) and the integral as the area under a curve (accumulation). Visual: Animation of a point sliding along a curve showing the changing slope, transitioning to the shading of an area growing under the curve.
sections.example: A squirrel gathering acorns: The rate of gathering (acorns/min) vs. total acorns accumulated.

sections.title: The Conceptual Link: Inverse Operations
sections.content: Define the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus as the realization that differentiation and integration are inverse processes, much like addition and subtraction. Visual: A 'Balance Scale' animation where putting an integral operator on one side and a derivative on the other keeps the original function in balance.
sections.example: A robot's position: If you know the velocity function, integrating gives you the position; if you have the position function, differentiating gives you back the velocity.

sections.title: The Accumulation Function
sections.content: Introduce the area function A(x) = ∫[a to x] f(t)dt. Explain that the rate at which this area grows is exactly equal to the height of the function at that point. Visual: A vertical line sweeping across a graph; as the line moves, the area 'paints' itself, and its growth rate is visualized as the height of the curve.
sections.example: Filling a water tank: The rate of water flow (f(t)) determines how fast the depth of the water (the area) increases.

sections.title: Formalizing the Connection
sections.content: Present the derivative of the accumulation function: d/dx [∫[a to x] f(t)dt] = f(x). Emphasize that this proves they are perfect opposites. Visual: An algebraic transformation showing symbols 'd/dx' and '∫' canceling each other out.
sections.example: A speedometer (derivative) vs. an odometer (integral): The speedometer measures the instantaneous change in distance recorded by the odometer.

sections.title: Summary & Application
sections.content: Recap that this relationship allows us to compute complex areas without infinite summations by simply finding the 'anti-derivative.' Visual: A split-screen showing a Riemann sum (many rectangles) instantly simplifying into a single subtraction problem [F(b) - F(a)].
sections.example: A space probe calculating its path: Using the known acceleration (derivative) to calculate the total distance traveled (integral) to reach a planet.
